pages.c33-p01: Define a robot, describe the sense-think-act cycle and give examples of different types of robot
pages.c33-p02: Describe the sensors robots use, how they move, and the meaning of degrees of freedom and accuracy

q.q: What is a robot?
o: A programmable machine that senses, decides and acts

q.q: What does the "think" step of a robot involve?
o: A program deciding what to do

q.q: Which is the "act" step for a robot vacuum?
o: A bump sensor detecting a wall

q.q: Which is the "sense" step for a robot arm?
o: A camera spotting a part on a conveyor

q.q: What is automation?
o: Machines doing tasks automatically that people once did

q.q: Which robot welds car bodies?
What is a cobot?
o: A collaborative robot that works safely beside people
q.why: Cobots stop if they touch people.

q.q: What is a humanoid robot?
o: A robot with a human-like body
A robot that is a human
q.why: Human-shaped robots work in human spaces.

q.q: Why are humanoid robots being trialled in factories?
o: They can work in spaces and with tools designed for people
They're cheaper than any other robot

q.q: Which is NOT usually called a robot?
q.why: It doesn't sense its surroundings or move itself.

q.q: Why is a remote-control car not really a robot?
o: A person makes all the decisions

q.q: How do surgical robots help surgeons?

q.q: What does an encoder count?

q.q: What does an IMU sense?

o: AI that lets computers understand images

q.why: Six lets it reach from many angles.

q.q: What is an end effector?
o: The tool on the end of a robot arm

q.q: Which end effector suits picking up flat boxes?
What does "repeatable" mean for a robot?
o: It does a task the same way many times

q.q: An echo returns after 0.01 s and sound travels at 340 m/s. How far away is the object?

o: The sound travels there and back

q.q: How does a quadcopter rise?
How does a quadcopter move forward?
o: The rear rotors speed up, tilting it forward
It uses a propeller at the back

q.q: What helps a drone hover still?
o: A flight controller making many tiny adjustments

q.q: Which drone camera helps find a missing walker at night?
How do drones help farmers?
o: Checking crop health and spraying only where needed

q.q: Why use drones for wind-turbine inspections?
o: Workers don't need to climb dangerous heights

q.q: Which is a real use of delivery drones?

You can see the drone yourself at all times
You watch on a phone screen only

q.q: Where must you never fly a drone?
o: In a large empty field (with permission)

q.q: Why must drone flyers respect privacy?
o: Drone cameras can film people without permission

q.q: What is an autonomous vehicle?
o: A car with a big engine
A car powered by the sun
A vehicle that can drive itself

q.q: What does "predict" mean for a self-driving car?
o: Working out what other road users will do next

q.why: Full self-driving in a set area.

What is an edge case?
o: A rare, unusual situation that's hard to handle
q.why: E.g. a horse on the road.

q.q: Which is an edge case for a self-driving car?
o: A police officer waving traffic through a red light

q.q: Why might rural roads be hard for self-driving cars?
o: Narrow lanes, poor markings and weak signal

q.q: Which is a possible benefit of self-driving cars?
o: Fewer crashes caused by human error

q.q: Which group could gain independence from self-driving cars?
o: People who can't drive, e.g. some disabled people

o: Farmers use robotic milking and drones, spending more time on planning and care

What does accountability mean?
Who might be accountable if a robot causes harm?
o: The maker, programmer, owner or user
q.why: Laws aim to make this clear.

q.q: How are cobots made safe?
o: They move as fast as possible
They slow down or stop when they touch a person

q.q: What is a "human in the loop"?

A person stuck in a loop

q.q: What is ethics?
o: Deciding what is right and wrong

q.q: Which is an ethical question about robots?
o: Should robots care for older people?

q.q: Which is an argument against care robots?
o: Residents may feel lonely without human contact

q.q: Which is an argument for warehouse robots?
o: They can work quickly and safely around the clock

q.q: What is an algorithm?
o: A precise set of steps to solve a problem

q.q: What is sequence?
What is selection?
o: Making a decision with IF ... THEN ... ELSE

q.q: What is iteration?
Why does a robot program usually loop forever?
o: So it keeps sensing and reacting

q.q: In "IF distance < 20 THEN stop", what is distance?
o: A sensor reading stored in a variable

q.q: How does a line-follower know it's on a black line?
o: Less light reflects back to its sensor

What is debugging?
What is a simulation?
o: A computer model used to test safely

q.q: Why might a robot behave differently in real life than in a simulation?
o: Wheels slip and sensor readings change

q.q: Which is a good debugging habit?
o: Change one thing at a time and record what happens

q.q: A robot turns too far. Which fix makes sense?
o: Reduce the turn time or angle and test again

q.q: What does the left-hand rule help a robot do?

Only a loop with no sensors

o: They may get in the way of pedestrians and wheelchair users

q.q: Which describes level 2 driver assistance?
o: The car steers and controls speed, but the driver must supervise
